Gnomon brings branching, field-level diffs, merge and undo to PostgreSQL.

[Install Gnomon](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/installation/) · [Tutorial](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/tutorial/) · [Product page](https://www.bitsinfra.com/gnomon)

**Fixed:**

- `stale_reads()`, `done()` and `merge()` raised `no_history_before_tracked` for a branch created before one of its tables was tracked, once a read on it had been recorded (#1). Such a read is now checked from the table's tracking point, which is what it saw. Read sets that 1.0.1 already recorded are fixed by the upgrade.
- A merge that wrote another branch (a three-way merge into main, which refreshes the source, or a merge into a branch) left the session's `gnomon.branch` on that branch until the end of the transaction. With the C module, later reads in the same transaction then read the branch instead of main, so a second merge in that transaction looked as if it had applied nothing. The session now stays where it was.
- With the C module, selecting a system column (`xmin`, `ctid`, `tableoid`) of a tracked table on a branch could crash the server. It is now refused with `system_column_on_branch`.

Install the TypeScript SDK with `npm install @bitsinfra/gnomon`, the Node binding with `npm install @bitsinfra/gnomon-postgres`, or the Python SDK with `python -m pip install gnomon-postgres`. The CLI archives cover macOS, Linux and Windows, and both Go modules are tagged at 1.0.2. The Ruby, Java, .NET, Elixir, PHP and dbt packages are attached below; each binding's page in the docs says how to install it.

The release includes SQL installers and upgrade scripts for existing 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 databases. The PostgreSQL image is available as `ghcr.io/bitsinfra/gnomon/postgres:v1.0.2` for Linux amd64 and arm64. See the installation guide for upgrade instructions.
